note: Reference renders exported by Filmora from projects written by Jibaru's .wfp writer. Media and exports live outside the repository (paths are on the machine that produced them).
paths: project, export, media and template paths are relative to `root` (the producing machine's scratch directory)

export.video: H.264, 1920x1080, 29.97 (30000/1001) fps, SDR Rec.709, Filmora 'Low' quality preset (6000 kbit/s target)
export.preset: Export > Local > Match to project settings, Quality Low; Auto Highlight task cancelled

gridA.desc: 10 s still test card: red->blue diagonal gradient, 16x9 numbered 120 px tiles (A0..A143), 10 px checker in alternate tiles, black grid lines, white circle (r 260) + letter A at centre, white/black corner squares, moving 8 px white marker on a black bar at y 1062-1080 (x = 6.4 px * source frame)

gridB.desc: same layout, green<->yellow anti-diagonal gradient, tiles B0..B143, letter B

sceneA.desc: Jibaru procedural sample scene A (mountain lake, pans right), 1920x1080

sceneB.desc: Jibaru procedural sample scene B (sunset sea, pans left), 1920x1080

media.encoding: libx264 crf 14, yuv420p, bt709, 300 frames at 30000/1001

layout.transition: one video track; clips alternate gridA/gridB, each playing its source from 3.003 s (handles for the transition); a cut every 2.5 s (more when a transition is longer), one transition per cut, centred on the cut, Filmora default 2.002 s; >= 0.5 s of plain clip between transitions. Item window = [start_s, end_s].
layout.effect: per item two 2.002 s clips with the effect at default parameters: gridA (source from 1.001 s) then sceneA (source from 1.001 s). Item windows grid_s / scene_s.

status_values.rendered: the window differs from the plain clips (max luma MAD > 2 at 160x90)
status_values.not_rendered: the window looks like the plain clips: Filmora did not apply the item from the project as written (writer cannot express it yet), or it is audio-only
status_values.not_exported: project built but not exported (disk space)
status_values.superseded: written with an upper-cased GUID (Filmora ids are case-sensitive) and not applied; re-rendered in the batch named by rerendered_in
